 Of the 24 IHSAA football teams remaining in the 2026 season , two reside in the South Bend area. Penn (6A) and Northridge (4A) both look to be amongst the final 12 tonight (Friday, Nov. 20) as they battle for semi-state championships and a spot in next weekend's state finals.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Both teams face stiff road challenges. No. 6 Penn (12-0) travels to No. 10 Carmel (8-4) in a Class 6A battle. While the Kingsmen were the higher-ranked team in the final USA Today Network poll and have an unbeaten record, Carmel is considered the favorite by most given its homefield advantage, tough regular season schedule and path to get here, which included an upset of No. 3 Westfield in the sectional opener.
 Meanwhile, No. 6 Northridge (13-0) visits No. 1 Fort Wayne Bishop Dwenger (12-1). While many expected Dwenger to be here at the beginning of the season given they are the defending 4A state champions, few outside Middlebury could have predicted the season the Raiders have had. After a pair of 3-win seasons, Northridge has set a single-season program record in wins already. Can they continue this magical run Friday night?
 More: Inside Penn football's first IHSAA 6A regional championship since 2017 
 More: Northridge football blasts Brickies to earn regional championship 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The South Bend Tribune will be covering both games, with Kyle Smedley at Penn-Carmel and Scott Davidson at Northridge-Dwenger. Make sure to come back to our site for extensive postgame coverage of both.
 In the meantime ...
 Below were our LIVE updates, scores and highlights from the Class 6A and Class 4A northern semi-state championship games.
